notes: The Pi model is not named in the manual. The 40-pin header is modelled as raspberry-pi-3b, which has the GPIO17 and GND port names.
The image highlights the GND pin (physical pin 9) and the GPIO17 pin (physical pin 11), so the black wire goes to GND.1 and the magenta wire goes to GPIO17.

The image labels the breadboard half that holds the buzzer as rows a-e, so I used catalogue bank 't' for it. The buzzer legs are in column 15 (black, negative) and column 18 (magenta, positive). Each wire is in row a of the same column, which is the same strip as the leg. The exact row of each buzzer leg is assumed to be e, but any row in the same strip is equivalent.
The buzzer is polarised: pin 1 (negative) goes to GND and pin 2 (positive) goes to GPIO17. The image shows the black wire on the negative leg.
No resistor is used, as in the tutorial.
